output.reply: The time frame is the player's own, so I am not picking it. Two new facts bear on it: cloud companies say running models is now a main reason they order accelerators, which suggests demand that outlasts one training cycle, while one large cloud company says it runs more of its work on its own chips, which sharpens the point against and the second wrong-if option.

findings.fact: Cloud companies said demand to run AI models, not only to train them, is now a main reason they order accelerators.
One large cloud company said it now runs more of its own AI work on chips it designs itself.
Orders driven by running models may recur beyond a single training cycle, which fits a window of about 30 sessions; this is an inference, and a source on how long those orders last is still needed.

A buyer shifting more of its work to chips it designs itself is the same risk the wrong-if option names, and it could build over a positional window; this is an inference from a single source, and how much work has moved is not disclosed.
